question.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,2,-6)$ and is parallel to the vectors $\mathbf{v_1}=\langle -3, 5, 2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{v_2}=\langle 1, 3, -2 \rangle.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,-6 \rangle.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $\mathbf{v_1}$ and $\mathbf{v_2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-16i-4j-14k \\  & =⟨-16,-4,-14⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =⟨-3,2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z-124 & =0 \\ 8x+2y+7z+62 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
